scenario.title: Elements: A River Worth Returning To
scenario.premise: Starting from four storybook elements, travel from an orchard to a coastal gathering. Make useful things for people you meet. The world remembers what you leave behind.

stage.title: Four beginnings
stage.speaker: The keeper
stage.motivation: The river gathering is a month away. We begin with earth, water, air and fire. Make a bowl for supper and bricks for a hearth.
stage.travelText: Our next stop: Four beginnings. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

things.label: Earth
things.description: Loose ground: mineral grit, clay and the material in which roots grow.

things.label: Water
things.description: Flowing, soaking and carrying; a liquid that takes the shape of its container.

things.label: Air
things.description: The invisible moving world around us. It carries moisture and feeds a flame.

things.label: Fire
things.description: Heat and light. It cooks, hardens and changes materials rather than merely joining them.

scenario.title: Elements: A River Worth Returning To
scenario.premise: Starting from four storybook elements, travel from an orchard to a coastal gathering. Make useful things for people you meet. The world remembers what you leave behind.

stage.title: The first boats are here
stage.speaker: The host
stage.motivation: The first visitors are here, dusty from the road and crossing. One holds out an empty cup; another asks where to wash. Make a washstand and a covered bottle of prepared water for them here at the gathering.
stage.travelText: The visitors step beneath the canopy and greet the neighbours who made it. The host introduces you before taking you to the washstand corner.

args: Stopped satisfied at the shared meal, stage 24. I expected practical combinations to help the arriving visitors; the washstand, filter chain and soap were mostly inferable. Water into a bowl and grain into a glazed bowl failed without explanation, so I used partner hints. The cooking-pot hearth error was particularly clear and useful. Making hot dishes and immediately seeing cooks serve them felt like a real payoff; I wanted to reach the table, not exhaust every recipe. The soap chain was competent but routine. Object persistence felt inconsistent: filling the same glazed bottle leaves the original empty bottle, while making seed oil removes the millstone. Combining compote and porridge also removed bread although I had not used it. I would stop comfortably here; mild curiosity about A gift for winter, not a strong urge to start another crafting chain. Logical interface only, not human or native UI evidence.
